summary: This October 12, 2023 article argues that education and human capital development are central to economic policy, linking global trends such as AI-driven personalized learning to local initiatives. It surveys local examples in green-tech training, industry-school partnerships, equity, skills-gap programs, new learning models, EdTech, entrepreneurship education and lifelong learning. The conclusion is that investing in human capital aligns communities with future markets.
one_line: Education and human capital policies, from local green-tech and EdTech programs to lifelong learning, are presented as drivers of local economic prosperity.
key_facts: The article is dated October 12, 2023 and argues human capital is an economy's greatest asset.
South Korea and Finland are cited as countries integrating artificial intelligence to customize student learning pathways.
Anne Cartwright, an education policy analyst, says lessons from challenging times are 'the cornerstones of future-focused educational policies.'
Mayor Jonathan Greenberg launched an initiative in Springfield on September 5, 2023 to build a workforce proficient in green technologies.
In Midvale, local tech companies work with public schools on curricula; Teresa Holmes is Director of Curriculum and Business Engagement.
Roanoke County announced upgrades to an online learning platform on November 17, 2023 to widen access to quality education.
The State of Jefferson unveiled an early childhood education initiative focused on literacy and numeracy.
Dr. Sarah Tan of the New Pathways Think Tank says 'The skills gap remains a pressing concern for local economies.'
Melville Community College introduced advanced robotics workshops reflecting regional manufacturing automation growth.
The Henderson District launched 'The Classroom Without Walls' on September 15, 2023, emphasizing experience over instruction.
The Metropolitan Borough of Carson plans substantial investment in virtual reality equipment for immersive learning in healthcare, engineering and urban planning.
Somerset County runs small business incubation programs tied to high schools, with students launching start-ups before graduation.
Dr. Marcus Liang argues an inclusive educational framework nurtures diverse talents integral to a robust economy.
Funding is being channeled to address the digital divide for rural and underprivileged urban communities.
